stanzas: 동해 물과 백두산이 마르고 닳도록,
하느님이 보우하사 우리나라 만세.
무궁화 삼천리 화려 강산,
대한 사람 대한으로 길이 보전하세.
남산 위에 저 소나무 철갑을 두른 듯
바람서리 불변함은 우리 기상일세.
가을 하늘 공활한데 높고 구름 없이
밝은 달은 우리 가슴 일편단심일세.
이 기상과 이 맘으로 충성을 다하여
괴로우나 즐거우나 나라 사랑하세.
orig.credit: Words of unknown authorship (1890s); the Korean text as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: Until the waters of the East Sea and Mount Baekdu dry up and wear away,
may God protect us: long live our country.
Mugunghwa, three thousand ri of splendid rivers and mountains:
people of Daehan, let us keep it long as Daehan.
Like that pine tree on top of Namsan, as if clad in iron armour,
unchanging through wind and frost: that is our spirit.
The autumn sky is wide and empty, high and without clouds;
the bright moon is our heart, single and true.
With this spirit and this heart, giving all our loyalty,
in suffering or in joy, let us love our country.
Donghae mulgwa Baekdusani mareugo daltorok,
Haneunimi bouhasa urinara manse.
Mugunghwa samcheolli hwaryeo gangsan,
Daehan saram Daehaneuro giri bojeonhase.
Namsan wie jeo sonamu cheolgabeul dureun deut
baramseori bulbyeonhameun uri gisangilse.
Gaeul haneul gonghwalhande nopgo gureum eopsi
balgeun dareun uri gaseum ilpyeondansimilse.
I gisanggwa i mameuro chungseongeul dahayeo
goerouna jeulgeouna nara saranghase.
rom.credit: Romanization: The Epoch Institute (Revised Romanization of Korean)

notes: line 1.1: the East Sea (Donghae) is the sea east of Korea; Baekdusan is the mountain on the border with China.
line 1.2: 'Haneunim', God or Heaven; 'bouhasa' is an archaic honorific form, 'may (He) protect'.
line 2.1: mugunghwa is the rose of Sharon (Hibiscus syriacus), Korea's flower; 'three thousand ri' is the traditional length of the country (a ri is about 400 m).
line 2.2: 'Daehan' (Great Han) is the country's name; literally 'Daehan people, as Daehan, long let us preserve (it)'.
line 3.1: Namsan, the mountain in the middle of Seoul.
line 4.2: 'ilpyeondansim', literally 'one piece of red heart': undivided loyalty.
